answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer:
Yes, skip it. A 16-miler on Wed Oct 14 would cost you on race day and give nothing back. A long run takes about two weeks to turn into fitness, and the race is four days after that Wednesday, so you would carry the fatigue and none of the benefit.

What you have banked is already enough. You ran 20 miles on Sep 13 and again on Oct 4, and you ran four straight weeks of 40 to 53 miles. Your easy pace and heart rate have not moved, which tells me you have not lost fitness.

The feeling of needing one more big run is common in race week. A short session at marathon pace on Wednesday gives you the race rhythm without the cost.

new.analysis:
You followed the plan exactly in the week of Oct 5 – 11. All five runs were done at the planned distance, both rest days were kept, and the marathon-pace session came in at 8:36/mi with no fade across the reps. Nothing needs correcting.

Your fitness is not slipping. Easy pace has held at about 9:52/mi at 139 bpm for four weeks, and the long runs built from 15 to 20 miles. One lighter week does not undo that.

Heavy legs a week out are common in a taper and usually lift over the last few days. You reported pain at 0/10 on every run and slept 7.5 hours a night, so nothing here points to a problem. The nervous feeling that you are losing fitness is also normal at this point.

The race moving two weeks earlier squeezed your taper, so the job this week is small. Keep a touch of race rhythm, cut the mileage to about 18 mi against 34 mi last week, and sleep well. Fatigue clears faster than fitness fades, which is why less running now makes you faster on Sunday.

Pacing will decide the race more than any workout now. Under 3:45 means 8:35/mi, which leaves almost no margin, so an even or slightly negative split is the safest route. Starting a few seconds slow costs very little. Starting fast costs a lot after mile 20.
